title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of Mendelian randomisation studies on dementia
author: Liam Seungjin Lee
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bpeemjbe
materials: Are outcome and exposure samples independent?
Are variants manually picked (e.g. to tackle pleiotropy)?
Is MR estimate compared with conventional observational estimate?

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Conduct a comprehensive search for primary MR studies using OVID and Web of Science across 13 databases (Medline, Embase, AMED, PsycINFO, BIOSIS Citation Index, Web of Science core collection, Current Contents Connect, Data Citation Index, Derwent Innovations Index, KCI-Korean Journal Database, Russian Science Citation Index, SciELO Citation Index, and Zoological Record).

substeps.instruction: Use OVID syntax: (exp Dementia/ or exp Cognition Disorders/ or dement* or alzheimer* or cognit* or neurocognit* or ((cognit* or memory or cerebr* or mental*) adj3 (declin* or impair* or los* or deteriorat* or degenerat* or deficit* or complain* or disturb* or disorder* or dysfunction* or insufficien* or fail*))) AND (exp Mendelian Randomization Analysis/ or (Mendelian adj1 random*) or (MR not (magnetic or resonance or imag* or receptor)) or (instrumental adj1 variable*) or (genetic adj1 instrument))
Use Web of Science syntax: TS=(dement* OR Alzheimer* OR cognit* OR neurocognit* OR memory OR cerebr* OR mental*) AND TS=(“Mendelian random*” OR “instrumental variable*” OR “genetic instrument*”)

steps.title: Screen Articles in Stage 1
steps.instruction: Assess article relevance based on title and abstract. Resolve uncertainties through discussion between two reviewers.

substeps.instruction: Include studies that are published or pre-print primary MR studies, have an outcome of any type of dementia, and investigate risk factors including systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, HDL, LDL, triglycerides, total cholesterol, BMI, diabetes, or plasma glucose (include tentatively if risk factors are not explicitly mentioned).
Exclude non-English articles, duplicates, and unavailable full texts.

steps.title: Screen Articles in Stage 2
steps.instruction: Further assess relevance by reading full texts accessed through an institutional library.

substeps.instruction: Include studies investigating systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, HDL, LDL, triglycerides, total cholesterol, BMI, diabetes, or plasma glucose.

Verify that the study reports a causal estimate value (odds ratio, hazard ratio, relative risk, or beta coefficient) using the inverse-variance weighted method in the main text or supplementary material.
Verify that the study reports a value for standard deviation, standard error, or 95% confidence interval in the main text or supplementary material.

steps.title: Perform Stage 3 Forward Searching
steps.instruction: Perform forward searching from selected studies to identify additional relevant studies.

substeps.instruction: Process any newly identified studies according to the Stage 1 and Stage 2 criteria.

steps.title: Extract Baseline Study Characteristics
steps.instruction: Extract specific data points for the selected studies.

substeps.instruction: General: title, year of publication, author, exposure(s), and outcome(s).
Exposure data: source article title and year, cohort, cohort inclusion/exclusion criteria, covariates, sex, SNP linkage disequilibrium r^2 cut-off, and number of SNPs.
Outcome data: source article title and year, cohort, case sample size, and control sample size.

steps.title: Perform Quality Assessment
steps.instruction: Evaluate studies using a questionnaire based on guidelines from Davies et al. (2018), Grover et al. (2018), and Burgess et al. (2020), focusing on the three main MR assumptions.

substeps.instruction: Assess if outcome and exposure samples are from the same ethnic population and are independent.
Evaluate Assumption 1: Evidence that variants are robustly associated with the risk factor.
Evaluate Assumption 2: Consideration of confounders between genetic variants and outcome.
Evaluate Assumption 3: Consideration of biological mechanisms other than the risk factor of interest.
Check if variants were manually picked (e.g., for pleiotropy) or pruned for independent instruments (linkage disequilibrium).
Verify if effect and other alleles are coded in the same direction for exposure and outcome (variable harmonization).
Check if MR estimate is compared with conventional observational estimate and if sensitivity analysis was performed.
Verify if data is available in a supplement or by request for reproduction.

steps.title: Conduct Quantitative and Qualitative Analysis
steps.instruction: Summarize data and perform meta-analysis using the R package 'meta'.

substeps.instruction: Standardize units to common units and convert standard errors to 95% CI.
Pool odds ratios (OR) from inverse-weighted variance analysis using a fixed effects model for each risk factor.
Generate a forest plot representing individual study ORs, overall estimates, and 95% CI.
Assess heterogeneity using I^2 statistics (0-25% low, 50-75% moderate, >75% high).
Perform 'one study removed' method if a study falls outside the 95% CI to check for skewing.
Assess publication bias using Funnel plots and Egger's regression.
